facts.statement: Paralitherizinosaurus was an extinct therizinosaurid theropod dinosaur found in the Upper Cretaceous Osoushinai Formation of Hokkaido, Japan.
facts.quote: Paralitherizinosaurus is an extinct genus of therizinosaurid theropod dinosaurs from the Upper Cretaceous Osoushinai Formation of Hokkaido, Japan.

facts.statement: The genus Paralitherizinosaurus contains only one known species, P. japonicus, which is known from a partial right hand and a cervical vertebra.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Paralitherizinosaurus japonicus, known from a partial right hand and cervical vertebra.

facts.statement: Paralitherizinosaurus is the youngest therizinosaur known to have lived in Japan.
facts.quote: Paralitherizinosaurus represents the youngest therizinosaur known from Japan.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen consists of a partial cervical vertebra, metacarpal I, the proximal ends of unguals I and II, and a nearly complete ungual III from the right hand.
facts.quote: The specimen consists of a partial cervical vertebra and the metacarpal I, proximal ends of unguals I and II, and nearly complete ungual III of the right hand.

facts.statement: Remains of this animal were first described by Murakami et al. in 2008 as an indeterminate maniraptoran theropod with possible therizinosauroid affinities.
facts.quote: Some of these remains were first described by Murakami et al. in 2008 as belonging to an indeterminate genus of maniraptoran theropod, possibly with therizinosauroid affinities.

facts.statement: Paralitherizinosaurus is the first named therizinosaur from Japan, though two other unnamed specimens of the group are known.
facts.quote: This taxon represents the first named therizinosaur from Japan, with two other unnamed specimens being known.

facts.statement: The genus name combines Greek words meaning "tidal" and "scythe" with the Latin word for "lizard".
facts.quote: The generic name, "Paralitherizinosaurus", combines the Greek words "paralos", meaning "tidal" and "therizo", meaning "scythe", and the Latin "sauros", meaning "lizard".

facts.statement: The species name "japonicus" refers to the animal's discovery in Japan.
facts.quote: The specific name, "japonicus", refers to the taxon's discovery in Japan.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses place Paralitherizinosaurus in an unresolved clade with Therizinosaurus, Suzhousaurus, and an unnamed therizinosaurid from Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: In their phylogenetic analyses, Kobayashi et al. (2022) recovered Paralitherizinosaurus as a member of an unresolved clade containing Therizinosaurus, Suzhousaurus, and an unnamed therizinosaurid from the Bissekty Formation of Uzbekistan.

facts.statement: Paralitherizinosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, between 83 and 75 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Paralitherizinosaurus japonicus es la única especie conocida del género extinto Paralitherizinosaurus de dinosaurio terópodo terizinosáurido que vivó a finales del período Cretácico, entre 83 a 75 millones de años, durante el Campaniense en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Fossils of Paralitherizinosaurus were found in Upper Cretaceous rocks of the Osoushinai Formation in Hokkaido, Japan.
facts.quote: Sus restos se hallaron en rocas del Cretácico Superior de la Formación Osoushinai en Hokkaido, Japón.

facts.statement: The time range for Paralitherizinosaurus is estimated to be between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Paralitherizinosaurus is classified within the family Therizinosauridae.
The genus Paralitherizinosaurus was established by Kobayashi et al. in 2022.
